title: Evaluation-normalized comparison of inverse pairing adjoints
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with chosen internal Homs $[U,V]$ and natural tensor-Hom adjunctions $\operatorname{Hom}(U\otimes V,W)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,[U,W])$. Write $U^\vee=[U,\mathbf1]$, $\operatorname{ev}_U:U\otimes U^\vee\to\mathbf1$, and for $f:U\to V$ let $f^\vee:V^\vee\to U^\vee$ be precomposition by $f$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a strong monoidal functor [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with $u:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\xrightarrow{\sim}F\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ and $\mu_{U,V}:FU\otimes FV\xrightarrow{\sim}F(U\otimes V)$.

Let $C,D\in\mathcal C$, $C',D'\in\mathcal D$, pairings $\beta:C\otimes D\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ and $\beta':C'\otimes D'\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$, an isomorphism $c:FC\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$, and a morphism $r:FD\to D'$ be given. Assume their tensor-Hom adjoints $b:D\to C^\vee$ and $b':D'\to(C')^\vee$ are isomorphisms. Suppose $h:F(C^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}(FC)^\vee$ is an isomorphism with
$$\operatorname{ev}_{FC}\circ(1_{FC}\otimes h)=u^{-1}\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\mu_{C,C^\vee},$$
and suppose
$$\beta'\circ(c\otimes r)=u^{-1}\circ F(\beta)\circ\mu_{C,D}.$$
No invertibility hypothesis is imposed on $r$.

Define $\ell=(c^{-1})^\vee\circ h:F(C^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}(C')^\vee$. Then
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(c\otimes\ell)=u^{-1}\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\mu_{C,C^\vee},$$
$$b'\circ r=\ell\circ F(b),\qquad r\circ F(b^{-1})=(b')^{-1}\circ\ell.$$
In particular $r=(b')^{-1}\circ\ell\circ F(b)$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $F(b^{-1})\circ\ell^{-1}\circ b'$. These are equalities of the specified maps, with the displayed strong monoidal unit and tensor constraints; the dual in $\ell$ is the dual of $c^{-1}$, not of $c$.

source.place: Second paragraph: perfect compact-support dual comparison, taking adjoints in the pairing square and inverting the horizontal adjoints; formal content of returned proof steps 5-6.

proof.text:
Write $\operatorname{uncurry}_A$ for the inverse of the stated tensor–Hom bijection with first tensor factor $A$. The evaluation and cancellation clauses of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], applied in $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$, give
$$\beta=\operatorname{ev}_C\circ(1_C\otimes b),\qquad \beta'=\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(1_{C'}\otimes b').$$
The same evaluation formula identifies $\operatorname{uncurry}_A(v)$ with $\operatorname{ev}_A\circ(1_A\otimes v)$ for every $v:T\to A^\vee$. Since uncurry is the inverse of a bijection, equality of these evaluations implies equality of the corresponding maps $v$. This last assertion uses injectivity of a bijection, not invertibility of any pairing comparison.

source.place: Final paragraph: taking adjoints in the commuting pairing square, then taking inverses of the horizontal adjoints.

proof.text:
Spell out precomposition, as defined in the statement. For $f:A\to B$, $f^\vee$ is uniquely characterized by
$$\operatorname{ev}_A\circ(1_A\otimes f^\vee)=\operatorname{ev}_B\circ(f\otimes1_{B^\vee}).$$
Indeed $f^\vee$ is the transpose $\operatorname{curry}(\operatorname{ev}_B\circ(f\otimes1_{B^\vee}))$, so the cancellation and evaluation clauses of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] give this equation, and uniqueness is injectivity of uncurry. Substitution of this equation twice and the tensor bifunctor law in [def-sfb-monoidal-category] give, for composable $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to E$,
$$\operatorname{ev}_A\circ(1_A\otimes(f^\vee\circ g^\vee))=\operatorname{ev}_E\circ((g\circ f)\otimes1_{E^\vee});$$
uniqueness under the stated adjunction gives $(g\circ f)^\vee=f^\vee\circ g^\vee$ and $(1_A)^\vee=1_{A^\vee}$. Put $d=(c^{-1})^\vee:(FC)^\vee\to(C')^\vee$ and $e=c^\vee:(C')^\vee\to(FC)^\vee$. The two inverse identities for $c$ now give $e\circ d=1$ and $d\circ e=1$. Thus $d$ is an isomorphism. Its defining evaluation equation, precomposed with $c\otimes1_{(FC)^\vee}$, gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(c\otimes d)=\operatorname{ev}_{FC},$$
since $c^{-1}\circ c=1_{FC}$.

source.place: Final paragraph: taking adjoints in the commuting pairing square, then taking inverses of the horizontal adjoints.

proof.text:
The composite $\ell=d\circ h$ is an isomorphism with inverse $h^{-1}\circ e$: both composite identities follow from Step 2 and the inverse identities of $h$. The tensor bifunctor law of [def-sfb-monoidal-category], Step 2, and the assumed evaluation normalization of $h$ give
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(c\otimes\ell)=\operatorname{ev}_{FC}\circ(1_{FC}\otimes h)=u^{-1}\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\mu_{C,C^\vee}.$$
This proves the first displayed conclusion with the specified unit constraint and the specified inverse variance of $c$.

source.place: Final paragraph: taking adjoints in the commuting pairing square, then taking inverses of the horizontal adjoints.

proof.text:
Compare the two proposed maps $FD\to(C')^\vee$ by evaluation. Using Step 1 and the tensor bifunctor composition law of [def-sfb-monoidal-category], the pairing-square hypothesis gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(c\otimes(b'\circ r))=\beta'\circ(c\otimes r)=u^{-1}\circ F(\beta)\circ\mu_{C,D}.$$
For the other map, Step 3 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(c\otimes(\ell\circ F(b)))
&=u^{-1}\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\mu_{C,C^\vee}\circ(1_{FC}\otimes F(b))\\
&=u^{-1}\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ F(1_C\otimes b)\circ\mu_{C,D}\\
&=u^{-1}\circ F(\beta)\circ\mu_{C,D}.
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is precisely tensorator naturality from [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] with $f=1_C$, $g=b$; the last uses functoriality and Step 1. No assumption on $r$ was used here.

source.place: Final paragraph: taking adjoints in the commuting pairing square, then taking inverses of the horizontal adjoints.

proof.text:
The inverse of $c\otimes1_{FD}$ is $c^{-1}\otimes1_{FD}$ by the tensor bifunctor laws of [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Precompose the equality of Step 4 with this inverse to obtain
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(1_{C'}\otimes(b'\circ r))=\operatorname{ev}_{C'}\circ(1_{C'}\otimes(\ell\circ F(b))).$$
The evaluation formula in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] identifies these as the uncurries of the two maps; injectivity of the stated adjunction bijection therefore gives $b'\circ r=\ell\circ F(b)$.

source.place: Final paragraph: taking adjoints in the commuting pairing square, then taking inverses of the horizontal adjoints.

proof.text:
Functoriality in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] gives $F(b)\circ F(b^{-1})=1$ and $F(b^{-1})\circ F(b)=1$. Postcompose the equality of Step 5 with $(b')^{-1}$ to get $r=(b')^{-1}\circ\ell\circ F(b)$. Precomposing this equality with $F(b^{-1})$ gives
$$r\circ F(b^{-1})=(b')^{-1}\circ\ell.$$
Finally put $s=F(b^{-1})\circ\ell^{-1}\circ b'$. Associativity and the displayed inverse identities give
$$r\circ s=(b')^{-1}\circ\ell\circ F(b)\circ F(b^{-1})\circ\ell^{-1}\circ b'=1_{D'},$$
$$s\circ r=F(b^{-1})\circ\ell^{-1}\circ b'\circ(b')^{-1}\circ\ell\circ F(b)=1_{FD}.$$
Thus $r$ is an isomorphism with exactly the claimed inverse, deduced from the pairing square rather than assumed.
